references.text: Moses exhorts Israel to fear the Lord and serve Him alone. The devil demands worship that belongs only to God, and Jesus answers with this verse in Luke 4:8.
The first commandment forbids having other gods. The devil's demand for worship is a direct violation of this fundamental commandment.
The parallel passage in Matthew where the devil offers Jesus all the kingdoms of the world if He will fall down and worship him. Matthew uses similar wording regarding worship (προσκυνήσῃς).
In Revelation, people worship the dragon (the devil) and the beast, showing that the devil's goal to receive worship is partially fulfilled in the end times.
Isaiah describes Satan's pride and his desire to ascend above God's stars and make himself like the Most High—the same desire to receive worship expressed in the temptation.
Israel is exhorted to fear the Lord, serve Him, and hold fast to Him alone. The devil's demand for worship stands in sharp contrast to this.
Jesus' answer to this temptation: 'Away from me, Satan! For it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him only shall you serve.' This directly rejects the devil's claim in Luke 4:7.
The Ten Commandments establish that God alone is to be worshipped, and that bowing down to other gods is forbidden. The devil's demand fundamentally breaks this rule.
